abertura: You are going to read the first email from a buyer who has not met you yet. Before you open it: this kind of message always does two jobs at once.
Mark the three statements that are true of a buyer's first approach.

itens.t: It asks for information and, at the same time, tests how you answer.
Everything it asks for is a question with a question mark.
The date in it is usually the most important line.
It is written so that a slow reply costs you nothing.
Some of what looks like a question is actually an offer.
It expects a formal document in return.

sec1.rationale: A first approach is short on purpose. What it asks for is easy to send; what it is really measuring is whether you answer, how fast, and whether you understood which of the three things mattered.

nota.texto: You told us the thing you would fix first is understanding what people are saying. This block starts one step earlier: with a message you already understand — and with what happens after you understand it. Reading is the strongest thing you have. Saying it back is the part that stops.

abertura: Choose the better reading for each expression. You will use all six in class.

itens.t: What they are asking is
alts: I am naming the request, in my own words
I am repeating their sentence
itens.ok: I am naming the request, in my own words

itens.t: They want to know whether
alts: this is a question about numbers
this is a yes-or-no question

itens.t: The deadline they gave is
alts: this is roughly when it would be nice to answer
this is when they need it, and it is not negotiable here
itens.ok: this is when they need it, and it is not negotiable here

itens.t: Let me make sure I have this right
alts: I am checking before I commit to an answer
I am apologizing for not understanding
itens.ok: I am checking before I commit to an answer

itens.t: The part I would answer first is
alts: I am ranking their questions, not just listing them
I am saying the others do not matter
itens.ok: I am ranking their questions, not just listing them

itens.t: What they are really proposing is
alts: I am guessing what they want
I am reading the offer behind the question
itens.ok: I am reading the offer behind the question

nota.texto: None of them adds information. Each one tells the other person what you are doing with what they said — naming it, checking it, ranking it, or reading what is behind it. That is why they buy you time without sounding like you need time.

doc.titulo: From: Diane Whitfield · Corporate Development, Halden Group
doc.texto:
Dear Caio,

I lead corporate development at Halden Group, and your company came up twice in our screening of data and AI services in Brazil. I would rather start with a short conversation than with a formal process.

Before we meet, three things would help us prepare. First, how your revenue splits between recurring managed services and project work. Second, how much of your delivery already runs in English for clients outside Brazil. And third — and I realize this may be premature — whether a minority investment is something you would consider at all, or whether you are only open to a full sale.

We are putting our shortlist together on Thursday, so anything you can send before then goes into it.

Best regards,
Diane Whitfield

abertura: Each line below comes from the email. What is it doing?

itens.t: "Your company came up twice in our screening."
"How your revenue splits between recurring services and project work."
"How much of your delivery already runs in English."
"Whether a minority investment is something you would consider."
"We are putting our shortlist together on Thursday."
"I would rather start with a short conversation."

nota.titulo: The minority-investment line is not a question
nota.texto: Whether a minority investment is something you would consider reads like the smallest of the requests. It is the largest: they are telling you what they might do, and asking you to react. The two data questions can be answered by anyone in your company. That one only you can answer.

sec4.titulo: Read it once more, for what it asks
abertura: Mark the three statements that are true of the email.

itens.t: It asks three things, and none of them is numbered.
It asks for a formal presentation of the company.
The date matters more than any single one of the three answers.
It says they are only interested in buying the company outright.
One of the three questions is about the language your team delivers in.
It asks you to reply after the shortlist is closed.

sec4.rationale: Three requests, one date, no numbering -- that is the standard shape. The date decides whether the other answers are worth anything, which is why it opens the reply.

nota.texto: The second question — how much of your delivery runs in English — is not small talk about your team. For a foreign buyer it is a risk question, and it is the one you are best placed to answer honestly and turn into a plan.

abertura: Each opening starts a particular kind of sentence. Complete it so it lands.

itens.t: What they are asking is
alts: for a formal proposal by Thursday
three things: revenue mix, delivery in English, and whether we would take an investment
why they contacted us in the first place
itens.ok: three things: revenue mix, delivery in English, and whether we would take an investment

itens.t: The deadline they gave is
alts: Thursday, when they close the shortlist
not clear from the email
next month, when we meet
itens.ok: Thursday, when they close the shortlist

itens.t: They want to know whether
alts: we would consider a minority investment or only a full sale
we have clients outside Brazil
our revenue is growing
itens.ok: we would consider a minority investment or only a full sale

itens.t: Let me make sure I have this right:
alts: you have already decided
you need this before Thursday, not after the call
you are making us an offer today
itens.ok: you need this before Thursday, not after the call

itens.t: The part I would answer first is
alts: none of them, until we meet
the investment question, because it is the only one they cannot get elsewhere
the revenue split, because it is the easiest
itens.ok: the investment question, because it is the only one they cannot get elsewhere

nota.texto: Saying which one you would take first is not avoiding the other two. It tells the buyer you read the email as a whole and you know which part is actually theirs to decide.

cl1.prompt: Which of these is saying it back -- and which is just repeating it?

itens.t: "You said that you lead corporate development at Halden Group and that our company came up twice in your screening."
"What you are asking is three things, and the third one is the one I can answer today."
"I read your email. It is very interesting. Thank you for contacting us."
"Let me make sure I have this right: you need this before Thursday, not after we meet."

cl1.rationale: Repeating gives the sender their own sentence back. Saying it back gives them your reading of it -- what you understood, in fewer words than they used.

abertura: A quick reference to the situation and the language you used.

tabela: A buyer's first email: three requests, one date, nothing numbered.
Saying back what they asked, in your own words, before you answer it.
What they are asking is… · They want to know whether…
Let me make sure I have this right…
The part I would answer first is…

callout.titulo: The one that does the most work
callout.texto: Let me make sure I have this right is not an apology and does not sound like one. It buys you a full sentence of thinking time and it makes the other person repeat the part that matters — which is exactly what you need when the call is live.

abertura: Record a short voice message, if you would like to.

callout.texto:
Take a real message you received this week — an email, a WhatsApp, a LinkedIn note.

What you are trying to do: say back what it asked, when they need it, and which part you would answer first. Ninety seconds, without reading it out.

abertura: Write the five-sentence version of that same reply -- one sentence per move.

callout.texto: Five is enough for any reply that fits in two minutes, and it is short enough that you will notice which move you skipped. Most people skip the date.
